stories.title: Twin Cities Apartments Sell in Deal Brokered by JLL
stories.excerpt: JLL has closed the sale of Twelve 501 Apartments, a 336-unit multifamily community in Burnsville, Minnesota. JLL represented the seller, FPA Multifamily and secured the buyer, Osso Capital, marking their first-ever investment in Minnesota. The JLL Capital Markets team was led by Managing Director Josh Talberg, Director Joseph Peris and Associate Eli Smith. “The asset’s quality, coupled with strong location fundamentals, makes this a standout investment and market entry-point for the Osso team,” said Talberg. “Twin Cities’ strong fundamentals continue to draw national attention, with ongoing new capital flows consistently entering the market.” Twelve 501 Apartments is located in Burnsville’s downtown corridor, featuring urban-style amenities and retail. Built in 1986 and extensively renovated beginning in 2017, the asset offers spacious layouts, plus a wide variety of community amenities. The four-story property is situated on a sprawling 14.62-acre site overlooking Birnamwood Golf Course. Stay ahead of the multifamily market at Connect Apartments. Gain firsthand insights from industry leaders on capital markets, development, operations, financing, and investment trends while expanding your network with the people making deals happen. See you on September 22! The post Twin Cities Apartments Sell in Deal Brokered by JLL appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Osso Capital acquires 336-unit Twelve 501 Apartments in Burnsville, Minnesota for first-time entry.
JLL closed sale; asset built 1986, extensively renovated 2017, located in downtown corridor.
Broker signals Twin Cities drawing sustained national capital inflows despite no purchase price disclosed.
stories.summary: JLL brokered the sale of Twelve 501 Apartments, a 336-unit community in Burnsville, Minnesota, to Osso Capital, marking their inaugural Minnesota investment. The four-story property, originally built in 1986 and comprehensively renovated starting in 2017, sits on 14.62 acres in Burnsville's downtown corridor with urban-style amenities. The broker's commentary emphasizes strong Twin Cities fundamentals attracting sustained new capital flows to the market.
stories.impact: Institutional capital seeking entry into Twin Cities multifamily signals confidence in Minneapolis-St. Paul's demographic and employment strength. A wave of first-time regional entrants into the market typically precedes rent growth acceleration and tightening of available stabilized assets—widening the window for ground-up development underwriting in high-growth submarkets before cap rates compress further.

stories.title: Healey Commits $93M to Capital Improvements at Springfield’s MassMutual Center
stories.excerpt: Massachusetts Gov. Maura Healey announced $93 million in new capital investments for Springfield’s MassMutual Center over the next five years. The commitment represents the largest investment in the facility’s history, according to the governor’s office. The improvements will modernize the arena and convention center, enhance accessibility and safety, improve the visitor experience, support the Springfield Thunderbirds, and strengthen the MassMutual Center’s role as a driver of economic activity for downtown Springfield and the region. The funding focuses on life safety and accessibility upgrades, improvements to the visitor experience and operational enhancements. “The MassMutual Center is an important economic engine for Springfield and all of Western Massachusetts, bringing visitors to the region, supporting local businesses and creating jobs,” said Healey. “This historic investment will modernize the facility, improve accessibility, enhance the experience for visitors and ensure the MassMutual Center remains a destination for conventions, sporting events, concerts and community gatherings for years to come.” The post Healey Commits $93M to Capital Improvements at Springfield’s MassMutual Center appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Massachusetts Gov. Healey commits $93M to MassMutual Center modernization over five years.
Funding targets life safety, accessibility, visitor experience, and supports Springfield Thunderbirds operations.
Investment framed as economic engine for downtown Springfield and Western Massachusetts region.
stories.summary: Governor Maura Healey announced $93 million in capital improvements for Springfield's MassMutual Center over five years, the largest investment in the facility's history. The funding covers life safety, accessibility, and operational upgrades while supporting the Springfield Thunderbirds and strengthening the venue's role as a regional economic driver for conventions, sporting events, and community gatherings.
stories.impact: Major civic/hospitality anchors rarely receive nine-figure modernization without accompanying downtown revitalization plans. This signals state intent to stabilize and attract foot traffic to Springfield's downtown core; multifamily developers should monitor for complementary TIF districts, tax abatements, or residential incentive programs that typically accompany such venue investments—creating near-term demand tailwinds for Class A rental housing adjacent to the arena.

stories.title: Slate Property Group Closes $1B Separately Managed Account for Secured Residential Loans
stories.excerpt: Slate Property Group said Friday it has closed on a new Separately Managed Account (SMA) with up to $1 billion of capital dedicated to sourcing and originating lower-leverage senior secured residential construction and bridge loans. Loans for residential developments in high-growth, transit-oriented East Coast markets will be the primary focus. “The new SMA complements and further diversifies our range of loan offerings across the capital stack and is a logical next step in our company’s continued evolution,” said Martin Nussbaum, co-founder and principal of Slate. “With this additional offering on the debt side, we look forward to being able to serve even more borrowers and continuing to catalyze new residential growth.” The SMA’s inaugural investment was a $45-million senior-secured construction loan for a new residential project located at 264-272 W. 135th St. in Harlem (pictured). The loan closed in July, helping to fund the ground-up construction of an 11-story, 72-unit building by Mass Development. The post Slate Property Group Closes $1B Separately Managed Account for Secured Residential Loans appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Slate Property Group closes $1B SMA for senior-secured residential construction and bridge loans.
Capital focused on high-growth, transit-oriented East Coast markets; inaugural $45M loan in Harlem.
Expanded debt offerings signal lender appetite for residential development despite tighter construction financing market.
stories.summary: Slate Property Group closed a $1 billion Separately Managed Account dedicated to lower-leverage senior-secured residential construction and bridge loans, with primary focus on high-growth, transit-oriented East Coast markets. The inaugural investment was a $45 million senior-secured construction loan for an 11-story, 72-unit ground-up development at 264-272 W. 135th Street in Harlem, funded in July.
stories.impact: Availability of fresh $1B construction capital earmarked specifically for East Coast transit-oriented residential indicates strong lender conviction in the product type and geography. This capital availability will stabilize construction loan pricing and terms, lowering development cost of capital and improving project feasibility in Northeastern submarkets—particularly valuable for mixed-income and urban infill projects competing for scarce transit-adjacent land.

stories.title: BXP Signs on as Development Advisor for Unfinished Oceanwide Tower in San Francisco
stories.excerpt: With the sale of the unfinished Oceanwide Plaza site in Los Angeles recently approved by a bankruptcy court, another project left in limbo by China-based Oceanwide Holdings’ collapse is gaining renewed momentum. The San Francisco Recovery Fund has hired BXP as a development advisor on plans to build a 910-foot mixed-use tower, the San Francisco Business Times reported. The fund purchased the Oceanwide development site at First and Mission, on which construction stalled in 2020, earlier this year. The nation’s largest publicly traded developer, BXP brings the developing horsepower and expertise to help bring the project to fruition, Dan Kingsley, co-founder of the Recovery Fund, told the Business Times. “As the largest commercial landlord in San Francisco and also the developer of the tallest building in San Francisco, we felt that [BXP] had unique insight into this market and what it would take to turn our concept for the First and Mission site into an actual development and occupied building,” Kingsley said. Pictured: The original design for Oceanwide Center. The post BXP Signs on as Development Advisor for Unfinished Oceanwide Tower in San Francisco appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: BXP hired as development advisor for stalled 910-foot mixed-use Oceanwide Tower in San Francisco.
San Francisco Recovery Fund purchased First and Mission site; construction halted since 2020.
BXP's expertise as largest SF commercial landlord and developer positioned to unlock value.
stories.summary: The San Francisco Recovery Fund, which acquired the stalled Oceanwide Plaza development site at First and Mission earlier this year, has hired Boston Properties (BXP) as development advisor to advance plans for a 910-foot mixed-use tower. BXP, the nation's largest publicly traded developer and San Francisco's largest commercial landlord, brings market expertise and development horsepower to revive the project that stalled in 2020 following Oceanwide Holdings' collapse.
stories.impact: Resolution of long-stalled trophy sites signals renewed capital confidence in San Francisco's downtown recovery post-pandemic. However, multifamily developers should note that BXP's appointment likely prioritizes office/commercial density over residential units—limiting direct supply competition but suggesting that residential-heavy competitors may face faster entitlement and leasing in alternative high-barrier SF submarkets as institutional capital refocuses on mixed-use trophy redevelopment.

stories.title: Lee & Associates Negotiates Pair of Industrial Lease Renewals in Itasca

Jeff Galante, SIOR, principal at Lee & Associates’ Illinois office, represented the tenant, Richards Building Supply, a national building exterior material supplier, in a 58,513-square-foot lease renewal at 909 W. stories.title: Spanish Hotel Operator Buys Chemists’ Club Hotel at 52 East 41st Street for $95M
stories.excerpt: A 107-key hotel in Midtown has traded for roughly $95 million. Eurostars Hotel Company, a Spanish hotel chain managing more than 300 properties globally, has purchased the Chemists’ Club Hotel at 52 East 41st Street from Azora, another Spanish company specializing in large-scale hotel investments, according to a source with knowledge of the deal. Eastdil Secured’s Jeffrey Davis and Scott Ellman arranged the deal for the seller, while it was unclear who repped the buyer. Eastdil declined to comment, while spokespeople for Eurostars and Azora did not immediately respond to requests for comment. The Real Deal first reported the news. It’s unclear when Azora acquired the 14-story hotel a block south of Grand Central Terminal, but the last trade recorded in property records was in 2007, when hotel chain Grupo Hotusa and Losan Hotels bought it for $77 million. Eurostars, which also owns the Eurostars Wall Street hotel at 129 Front Street in the Financial District, is a subsidiary of Grupo Hotusa, so the Midtown property is returning to its previous roots. The property was built around 1910, but not as a hotel. The building was originally the site of the historic headquarters of the Chemists’ Club, a prominent social and dining hub for leading scientists and industry pioneers. The building was later redeveloped by fortuna realty group in 1997 and opened in 2000 as the Dylan Hotel. Last year, it was again heavily redesigned and rebranded, and officially opened as the Chemists’ Club Hotel. The hotel is currently home to Benjamin Steakhouse on the ground floor and features amenities such as a lounge bar, coworking spaces and a fitness center. News of the sale comes after a slew of other hotel sales in Manhattan recently. In June, Meliá Hotels International bought the 12-story hotel at 132-142 West 27th Street in NoMad for $203 million, while Omni Lifestyle Living acquired a Marriott hotel at 21 West 37th Street in Midtown for $39.9 million, also in June. bullets: Eurostars Hotel Company (Spanish operator) acquires 107-key Chemists' Club Hotel for ~$95M.
Property at 52 East 41st Street, Midtown Manhattan; Eurostars subsidiary of Grupo Hotusa.
Last major trade recorded in 2007 at $77M; ownership returning to parent company.
stories.summary: Eurostars Hotel Company, a Spanish hotel chain managing over 300 properties globally, purchased the Chemists' Club Hotel, a 107-key property at 52 East 41st Street in Midtown Manhattan, from Azora for approximately $95 million. The 14-story hotel, built around 1910, returns to roots of its previous owner Grupo Hotusa. Eastdil Secured arranged the deal for the seller.
stories.impact: Hospitality acquisition; no direct relevance to multifamily residential development, supply, demand, or capital flows.

stories.title: Izo Capital Lends $26M on Wyoming Apartments Near Jackson Hole
stories.excerpt: Sundance Properties has sealed $25.6 million of construction financing to bring a multifamily development in Alpine, Wyo., across the finish line, Commercial Observer has learned. Izo Capital supplied the 24-month senior construction loan to fund the completion of Phase 1 of the developer’s planned the Flats at Alpine Junction project comprising 64 units. The debt will support the completion of three additional buildings comprising 48 apartments on top of 16 units that are already completed and leased. Peter Porraro, co-founder and chief investment officer at Izo Capital, said the overall project, which will eventually total 160 units, is set up for success given that it’s 35 miles from Jackson Hole mountain valley, with a number of employers based in the town of Jackson, Wyo. Porraro noted that Alpine also has demand drivers for multifamily with limited supply coupled with a newly opened medical center and a public charter school scheduled to open for the 2026-2027 academic year. “It’s very hard to develop out there, and it’s hard to get the infrastructure,” Porraro told CO of the need for more apartments projects near Jackson Hole. “There’s just no supply and nothing new in the market.” The Flats development has already shown strong leasing momentum, according to Porraro, with the current rental rates helping support underwriting assumptions in the loan for the remaining phases of the project. The first phase is slated for completion next spring. Porraro noted that there is large-scale demand for rental housing for those who work in Jackson Hole given that median home prices in the city are close to $3 million, with townhomes starting at around $1 million. He said the project at 303 Highway also benefits from transportation connectivity that includes direct access to the START Bus system linking Alpine and Jackson. “The demand we’ve experienced from the first completed building reinforces the critical need for new rental housing in Alpine,”
bullets: Izo Capital provides $25.6M construction financing to Sundance Properties for Alpine, Wyoming apartments.
Flats at Alpine Junction Phase 1: 64 units total; 16 completed/leased, 48 in construction.
Project benefits from Jackson Hole proximity (35 mi), local employers, new medical center, charter school opening 2026-27.
stories.summary: Izo Capital closed a $25.6 million, 24-month senior construction loan to Sundance Properties for Phase 1 of the Flats at Alpine Junction, a 64-unit development in Alpine, Wyoming. The loan funds completion of three additional buildings (48 units) on top of 16 already completed and leased units. The overall project is planned to reach 160 units and benefits from proximity to Jackson Hole employment centers, a newly opened medical center, and a public charter school opening in 2026-27.
stories.impact: Lender conviction in small-market multifamily near resort/destination economies signals that constrained supply (difficult development environment) plus employment/institutional anchors (medical center, school) create defensible rental demand. Alpine's limited supply and amenity additions (medical, education) should support near-term rent growth; developers with land control near Jackson Hole or similar resort-adjacent mountain communities should accelerate entitlement and construction financing conversations while labor and materials availability remain adequate.

stories.title: CW Realty Closes Deal to Buy 55 Smith Street in Downtown Brooklyn for $58M
stories.excerpt: CW Realty Group closed on a deal to acquire a parking facility in Downtown Brooklyn, Commercial Observer has learned. Cheskie Weisz’ CW Realty entered into a contract to purchase 55 Smith Street in December from New Jersey-based firm Edison Properties, Crain’s New York Business reported at the time. The sale closed on Friday and its price was disclosed at $58 million, according to broker JLL. CW Realty has not disclosed any specifics about their plans for the site, which has an alternative address of 160 Livingston Street, but the lot spans 13,707 square feet and is one of the biggest residential development opportunities in Downtown Brooklyn, the JLL Capital Markets team said. “This transaction demonstrates the strength of demand for well-located development opportunities across New York City, particularly in neighborhoods with strong residential fundamentals and supportive zoning,” JLL’s Mike Mazzara, who negotiated the deal alongside Ethan Stanton, Brendan Maddigan and Drew Isaacson, said in a statement. “The site offers a combination of scale, flexibility and development incentives in one of Brooklyn’s most dynamic neighborhoods.” CW Realty and Edison Properties did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Developers can build 137,000 square feet on the site as of right or 164,000 square feet under the Universal Affordability Preference program with no height limits or parking requirements for a potential housing development. CW Realty has the option to build using the city’s 485-x program and benefit from reforms made under the City of Yes for Housing Opportunity. An added bonus is that development on the site is not restricted to rental housing or condominiums, according to JLL. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: CW Realty closes $58M acquisition of 55 Smith Street parking facility in Downtown Brooklyn.
13,707 sf site; one of largest residential development opportunities in Downtown Brooklyn; use undisclosed.
JLL highlights strong zoning, scale, and residential fundamentals supporting development optionality.
stories.summary: CW Realty Group closed the acquisition of 55 Smith Street (also known as 160 Livingston Street), a 13,707-square-foot parking facility in Downtown Brooklyn, for $58 million from Edison Properties. JLL, which brokered the deal, described the site as one of Downtown Brooklyn's largest residential development opportunities, noting strong zoning, scale, and supportive residential fundamentals, though CW Realty has not disclosed specific redevelopment plans.
stories.impact: A major New York developer's $58M land acquisition at significant per-square-foot basis signals confidence in Downtown Brooklyn's residential absorption and pricing power. The aggressive land purchase (likely for ground-up residential redevelopment) before announcing plans suggests CW Realty sees a narrow window for entitlement and financing in a tightening market; this should push competing developers to accelerate Downtown Brooklyn underwriting and land acquisition strategies, particularly around transit nodes, before comparable land prices escalate further.

stories.title: Kimco Buys Two Broward Retail Centers for $109M
stories.excerpt: Kimco Realty, one of the biggest owners of grocery-anchored retail centers in the country, has acquired two more in Broward County for a combined $109 million from KPR Centers, property records show. In the largest transaction, the Jericho, N.Y.-based REIT paid $56 million for Sunshine Plaza, a 245,744-square-foot property between 4017 and 4299 West Commercial Boulevard in Tamarac, just east of the Florida’s Turnpike. Publix and Marshalls anchor the 19-acre shopping center. Other tenants include Crunch Fitness, Krispy Kreme and Subway. New York-based KPR had purchased the property for $28.5 million in 2014. In the smaller trade, Kimco Realty paid $53 million for the 254,749-square-foot Pompano Marketplace at 1115 and 1117 South Federal Highway. It also spans about 19 acres, with a Walmart Neighborhood Market as the anchor. Other tenants include Ross Dress for Less, Carrabba’s Italian Grill and TD Bank. KPR Centers had purchased the asset for $46.8 million in 2015. Kimco Realty owns 589 properties nationwide, including 44 across South Florida. In one of South Florida’s largest retail deals in recent years, the REIT paid $216 million for The Shops at Mary Brickell Village in Miami in 2022. Representatives for Kimco Realty and KPR Centers did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Kimco Realty acquires two Broward County retail centers from KPR Centers for combined $109M.
Sunshine Plaza (Tamarac): $56M, 245,744 sf, Publix/Marshalls anchored; Pompano Marketplace: $53M, 254,749 sf, Walmart Neighborhood Market anchored.
KPR Centers purchased same properties for $28.5M and $46.8M in 2014-2015; significant value appreciation.
stories.summary: Kimco Realty acquired two grocery-anchored retail centers in Broward County from KPR Centers for $109 million. Sunshine Plaza in Tamarac (245,744 sf, Publix/Marshalls anchored) sold for $56 million, while Pompano Marketplace (254,749 sf, Walmart Neighborhood Market anchored) sold for $53 million. KPR Centers had purchased the same properties for a combined $75.3 million in 2014-2015.
stories.impact: Retail-focused transaction with minimal direct relevance to multifamily development; however, sustained REIT appetite for grocery-anchored centers in South Florida may indicate broader investor confidence in the region's population/demographic stability, which could support parallel multifamily thesis in Broward submarkets.

stories.title: Schuckman Buys Northeast Queens Shopping Center for $56M
stories.excerpt: Punia & Marx Real Estate sold the Whitestone Shopping Center in Queens for $56 million. BTF Capital Fund, led by Kenneth Schuckman and Aaron Malinsky, purchased the Key Food-anchored property at 153-15 Cross Island Parkway, according to a deed transfer in property records filed Friday. The purchase could be a play for assets tied to grocery stores and other necessity-based retail. Schuckman’s brokerage firm, Schuckman Realty, will handle leasing for the shopping center, according to the buyer. Acadia Realty Trust provided about $48.5 million in financing to Schuckman for the acquisition through a shell corporation, with Acadia’s Chief Financial Officer John Gottfried signing the mortgage documents. Punia & Marx and Acadia did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Punia & Marx has owned the property since at least 1975, and the amount paid for that acquisition is unknown. Schuckman seems to have been involved in the management operations of the 220,000-square-foot shopping center, which is also leased to a Chase Bank branch, with a 2020 flier listing Kenneth Schuckman and Jessica Vilmenay as exclusive brokers. The advertisement said at the time that a redevelopment of the property would be taking place, but was not specific about the nature of the repositioning. Schuckman promoted the center based on 100,000 cars passing by the center daily on the Cross Island Parkway and 333,000 people living within three miles. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: BTF Capital Fund (Schuckman/Malinsky) acquires 220,000 sf Whitestone Shopping Center for $56M.
Key Food-anchored property at 153-15 Cross Island Parkway, Queens; owned by Punia & Marx since 1975.
Acadia Realty Trust provided ~$48.5M financing; Schuckman Realty to handle leasing operations.
stories.summary: BTF Capital Fund, led by Kenneth Schuckman and Aaron Malinsky, purchased the Whitestone Shopping Center in Queens for $56 million from Punia & Marx Real Estate. The 220,000-square-foot, Key Food-anchored property at 153-15 Cross Island Parkway also features Chase and other necessity-based tenants. Acadia Realty Trust provided approximately $48.5 million in acquisition financing.
stories.impact: Retail-focused acquisition; minimal direct relevance to multifamily development demand and supply dynamics, though continued grocery-anchored retail investment in outer-borough Queens may reflect demographic stability supporting parallel multifamily demand in transit-accessible neighborhoods.
